# Cache lookup that also remembers missing links

> `getOrLoad` is a cache lookup that stores a link for an hour, serves old copies while it refreshes, and briefly remembers that a code was not found.

_Part of [Look up a code through Bloom filter, cache and DynamoDB](resolve-pipeline.md)_

`resolve` in [`ShareLinkService`](link-click-analytics.md) calls `getOrLoad` on the shared [`CacheService`](../../../../packages/backend/libs/infrastructure/cache/cache.service.ts#L48) after the format check and the Bloom filter have let a code through (see [Look up a code through Bloom filter, cache and DynamoDB](resolve-pipeline.md)). You pass it a cache key, a loader function, and a few timing options. The key comes from `linkCacheKey`, which builds `link:v1:<code>`. The `v1` is a version tag, so the key layout can change later without reading old entries. On a cache hit, you get the stored link right away. On a miss, `getOrLoad` runs the loader. The loader does a DynamoDB `GetCommand` on the `Links` table and returns the item, or `null` if there is none. The result goes into the cache for 1 hour. After that hour, the old copy can still be served for up to 24 hours while a refresh happens (stale-while-revalidate), so a slow DynamoDB does not slow down the redirect. A `null` result is cached too, but only for 60 seconds. That is the negative cache. Repeated lookups for a code that does not exist skip DynamoDB. The short timer means a mistake fixes itself quickly. When `create` claims a code, it calls `cache.invalidate` on the same key. That drops any cached "not found" for a just-claimed alias. Back in `resolve`, an expired link is still dropped after the cache returns it, because expiry is checked on the returned value.

**Look at:** [`resolve` in share-link.service.ts](../../../../packages/backend/libs/domains/marketing/application/share-link.service.ts#L41) · [`linkCacheKey` in share-link.service.ts](../../../../packages/backend/libs/domains/marketing/application/share-link.service.ts#L35)

## Pieces

- Cache key for one link, versioned: `linkCacheKey` turns a code into `link:v1:<code>`, and `create` uses the same key to clear stale entries.
- Fresh time, stale time and not-found time: The options passed to `getOrLoad` are 1 hour fresh (`ttlMs`), 24 hours stale-while-revalidate (`swrMs`), 60 seconds for a cached miss (`negativeTtlMs`), and a `hot` in-process layer (`l1`).
- Loader that reads one link from DynamoDB: A function that does a `GetCommand` by `code` on the `Links` table and returns the item or `null`.

## What it touches

| Kind | Name | How |
|---|---|---|
| cache | `link:v1:<code>` | Holds the link, or a remembered "not found", read and filled through `getOrLoad` and cleared by `create`. |
| database | `Links (DynamoDB)` | The loader reads one item by `code` when the cache has nothing usable. |

## Watch out

- A missing code is cached for only 60 seconds, so a freshly created link or alias can look missing for up to a minute unless `create` clears the key, which it does.
- Stale data can be served for up to 24 hours while a refresh runs, so edits to a link may not show up instantly.
- Expiry is checked after the cache returns, so a link with `expiresAtEpoch` in the past can sit in the cache but still resolves to `null`.
- Changing the key layout means changing `v1` in `linkCacheKey`, since old entries are otherwise read as-is.
